title: Structured video calls for delirium prevention in the intensive care unit with family members
summary: Severely ill intensive care patients sometimes experience strong states of confusion. Contact with familiar people may help reduce this. This study examines whether short, daily video calls between patients and family members during the ICU stay are practical to carry out and may help prevent such confusion.
conditions: Delirium, not induced by alcohol and other psychoactive substances

interventions.name: Patients in the intervention group receive structured daily video calls with a family member, in addition to standard intensive care treatment. The video calls take place throughout the duration of the ICU stay, with a planned maximum duration of 20 minutes per call at a fixed time of day (between 5

Patients in the control group receive standard intensive care treatment without a structured video-call protocol. Contact with family members follows the ward's usual visiting and communication practices.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Expected ICU length of stay > 48 hours
RASS (Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale) −2 to +3
No active delirium at study enrollment
Sufficient German language proficiency
Availability of a family member able to provide consent
Availability of a private video-call-capable device (also on the family member's side)
Exclusion criteria:
Pre-existing severe cognitive impairment
No available family member
End-of-life / palliative situation
ICDSC (Intensive Care Delirium Screening Checklist) positive at enrollment
Aphasia
Severe hearing or visual impairment
No private video-call-capable device available
